ImageDescription.value: A 1915 Ford Model T Runabout in the Petersen Automotive Museum.

The Ford Motor Company was established in 1903, The Model T Ford was built from 1908-1927, a few models were built before the Model T, but the T was the first mass produced car. Ford wanted to keep the price low as possible, so to increase efficiency, he was the first to use assembly line production. Ford also made use of the knock-down kit concept, so almost from the beginning, the Model T was built in many other countries as well as the US, such as England and Australia. The first car imported to Australia was the Model A in 1904, The Model T imported from 1909. From 1925, Fords were assembled in Geelong, Australia. The Model T slowly developed over its production life; 1909-14 T1; Flat top hood, flat cowl below the screen and gas lights. 

                  Cars from 1913 to 14 had the dog leg windscreen

1915-16 T2; had louvres in hood, contoured cowl and electric lights.. 1917-23 T3; The hood tapered with a curved top, hinges moved. 1923-25 T4; Angled Screen, taller and wider at firewall. 1926-27 T5; Wire wheels, cowl now similar to Model A.

The Model T Speedster was the original fast Ford, not long after the introduction of the Model T, a market quickly arose for parts to make your car go faster, such as hot up engine parts and sleek body kits.

ImageDescription.value:
The Model T Ford was built from 1908-1927. The Ford Motor Company was established in 1903, a few models were built before the Model T, but the T was the first mass produced car. Henry Ford wanted to keep the price low as possible so every middle class American could afford one, so to increase efficiency, he was the first to use assembly line production. Ford made use of the knock-down kit concept, so almost from the beginning, the Model T was built in other countries as well as the US, such as England and Australia. In Australia Ford cars were supplied by Ford Canada to avoid extra import duties imposed on non-Empire produced goods. They were originally shipped virtually complete, but as the number of local body building operations grew motor cars were increasingly delivered as CKD form. 

1909-14 T1; Flat top hood, flat cowl below screen and gas lights.
    Cars from 1913 to 14 had the dog leg windscreen

1915-16 T2; louvres in hood, contoured cowl, electric lights.. 1917-23 T3; Hood tapered with a curved top, hinges moved. 1923-25 T4; Angled Screen, taller and wider at firewall. 1926-27 T5; Wire wheels, cowl now similar to Model A. From 1914-26 Model Ts were "any colour so long as it is black"

Engine; 20hp 177 Cu in

45448580.title: File:1915 Ford Model T The Grasshopper (21525153999).jpg

ImageDescription.value:
John Geraghty built the Grasshopper in the late 1950s, it featured on the cover of the 1959 issue of HOT ROD magazine. A custom chassis housed a 4-71 GMC-blown 303ci Olds V8 (punched to 350 ci), La Salle transmission, and a Halibrand quick-change rear axle. All of this was draped with a removable 1915 Model T body, painted translucent glamour green lacquer, It delivered more than 800 hp, running Irwindale’s quarter-mile in the low 9s at 150-plus mph. Sadly over the years, the Grasshopper was parted out. This is a recreation of that famous hotrod, built by Dave Shuten, on display at Galpin Auto Sports.

Read more: www.hotrod.com/news/1506-legendary-grasshopper-builder-jo...

ImageDescription.value: Ford Model T Touring 1915

The 1915 Ford Model T Touring was a popular and affordable open-bodied car for families, a significant step in the mass production of automobiles. Around 308,000 Model T's were produced in 1915 alone, with the touring body style being the most popular.
